book_title: Building Agentic AI Systems: From First Agent to MCP, Multi-Agent Orchestration, and Production
author: Srinivasa Rao Bittla

offline_test_status.model: scripted stand-in (solutions/tests/fakemodel.py); no API key, no model provider called

model_test_status.evidence: solutions/outputs/*/summary.json (each records its own commit and lock hash)

known_limitations: Live-model runs were recorded on earlier commits than the verified one; each summary.json names its own commit.

Two runtime images come from other publishers and are pinned by digest: the GitHub MCP server v1.12.2 (exercises 14.3, 14.4, Capstone 4) and Ollama 0.34.4 (the free local model). If a registry stops serving them, see VERSION_MATRIX.md.
Production readiness is not claimed: the course kit is not production-hardened (Appendix M of the book, SECURITY_MODEL.md).
open_gates: Live-model runs come from 7 commits; rerun them on the release commit, or record for each exercise why its evidence still applies.
Clean setup from a fresh checkout on Windows, macOS and Linux (./course.sh setup, build, selftest, quickstart).
Independent technical review and a beginner-reader pilot (PILOT.md), with findings recorded.
Final proof of the print files, and KDP preview of paperback and hardcover (trim, gutter, spine, cover, ISBN and metadata).
Confirm the ISBN registrations match the title, subtitle, author and imprint.
Run dev/check_links.py with network access on the release commit, and open by hand any link a site blocks for automated checks (403) or rejects for its user agent.
Publish the book-v1.0.0 tag on the verified commit (or a docs-only commit after it), then check that a clean checkout of the tag follows How to Use This Book's setup exactly.
commit_note: git_commit is the commit the tests ran on. The release tag may sit on a later commit that adds only verification artifacts and docs; release_manifest.py --check fails if any code, solution, test or environment file changed in between.
